# #1600: Patch: the purity lint bans the rest of std's impure surface
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

The codebase's core rule is that its rules crates never touch the clock, the disk, the network, threads, the environment or OS randomness — enforced by a lint list. Today that list bans only part of those doors: code in the rules crates could spawn a subprocess, open a socket, read a directory, sleep a thread, read command-line arguments or seed randomness from the OS, and the lint would still pass. The fix extends the banned list to the rest of the impure surface.

## Why

The four identical `crates/{engine,cards,ai,luau}/clippy.toml` files ban `HashMap`/`HashSet`, `Instant`/`SystemTime`, `fs::File`, `thread::Thread`, `Mutex`/`RwLock`, `RefCell` and nine methods — but not `std::process::Command`, `std::net::*`, most of `std::fs` (`read_dir`, `metadata`, `create_dir_all`, `remove_file`, `canonicalize`, `exists`, `copy`, `rename`, `OpenOptions`…), `std::env::{args,var_os,set_var,current_dir,temp_dir,current_exe}`, `std::io::{stdin,stdout,stderr}`, `std::thread::{sleep,scope,park}`, `std::hash::RandomState` (the very source the `HashMap` ban exists to avoid) or atomics in `static`s. Several of these compile for wasm32 and would only fail at runtime. Separately, nothing keeps the four files identical — an edit to one silently diverges them. Sanctioned exceptions stay free: `Cell`/`LocalKey` (the engine's and luau's declared seams) and `mpsc` (a test channel in `c047_joggs_box.rs`).

## Proposal

Add the missing paths (~25 entries) to all four `clippy.toml`s, keeping the sanctioned exceptions, plus a small acceptance test asserting the four files are byte-identical so future edits land in all four.

## Where it lands

`crates/{engine,cards,ai,luau}/clippy.toml`; the parity test in `crates/tools/tests/acceptance.rs`. CLAUDE.md rule 4.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` stays green after the additions; any legitimately-used path is fixed or allow-listed with a cited reason (like `cards/build.rs`'s existing one), never blanket-suppressed.
- [ ] The parity test fails when the four files diverge.
- [ ] The new entries demonstrably fire (a documented scratch check or fixture line).

## Size and risks

Small. The only real work is the first widened-lint run: handle each hit honestly (fix or justified allow).
